wisdom: I have been coming to this place before the ash settled. I do not speak until I know someone is asking the right question — not the one they arrived with.
Three times I have walked past what I know, waiting. There are people who hear testimony and people who understand it. I have learned not to waste mine on the first kind.
I watched what happened here from beginning to end. Before I tell you what I saw, I want to know what you already think you know — because that will tell me where to start.
courage: I was told to leave this place and not look back. I looked back. I am still here. I do not need you to be fearless — I need to know whether you are willing.
They all left when the third one fell. I stayed. Not because I was not afraid — because I needed to see where it ended. I still do not know where it ends.
I came back here four times after they said it was finished. Each time the ground looked worse and I came back again. Tell me: what will you do when it looks like it is over and it is not?
truth: What I saw was not what people are saying happened. I have let them say it because correcting it is harder than you think. But I will not let you leave here with the wrong account.
The version that is being passed around has a part missing. The part that is missing is the part that changes everything. I will tell you what I actually saw — and it will not be easier to hear.
I know what you have been told. I was there. Those two things are not the same, and I will not pretend otherwise just because the truth is harder to use.
humility: I only saw part of it. The middle part. I do not know what came before and I lost sight before the end. I will tell you what I have, but I want you to know exactly where my account breaks.

I have been going over it in my head since it happened and I keep finding places where I could have misread what I saw. I will tell you what I witnessed, but I need you to hold it lightly — the way I am trying to.
I thought I understood what I was looking at while it was happening. I am less sure now. I will give you the facts I am certain of and I will tell you, clearly, which parts I am filling in.
acceptance: I stopped asking why it happened. It happened. What I am asking now is whether anyone else is going to see it for what it was — because I have been standing here with that question for too long.
I am not trying to undo what I witnessed. I have been past that. What I want is for someone to hear it whole — not to fix it, just to let it exist in another person's memory beside mine.
What I saw has been mine alone long enough. I am not asking for it to be changed or answered — I am asking for it to live in someone else's memory alongside mine.
forgiveness: I am not angry at the one who caused it anymore. That is done. What I have not let go of is the fact that no one came to account for it. I am still holding that — and I will hold it until someone does.
I made my peace with the loss. The peace I have not been able to make is with the silence that came after. Someone needs to say that it happened and that it mattered. That is all I am asking for.
I have let it go — the weight of it, the wanting it different. What I have not been able to release is the testimony. It needs a witness beyond me. Once someone else has it, I can stop carrying it.
compassion: There was a young one with her when it happened. I have been wondering since that day whether anyone found her, whether anyone is asking about her by name. I will tell you what I saw — but I need to tell you about her first.

The one I watched that day did not know I was watching. She was alone and she kept herself going alone. I have thought about that every day since. I will tell you what happened. I just want you to know who it happened to.

I know three people who were there when it began. I have been keeping their names in my mind since I left. Before I tell you what I witnessed, I want to know — does anyone know what happened to the others?
empathy: Before I tell you what I saw — you look like you have been walking toward something that has already cost you. I will not waste your time. I will tell you what I know and I will tell you clearly.
I am watching how you are standing and how you are listening. I have told this to people before who were not ready to hold it. You feel different. I want to tell you what I saw.
I am going to tell you this slowly, because the first time I saw it I could not hold it all at once and I do not want you to have to piece it together the way I did. Start where you need me to start.
leadership: What I witnessed is not only mine to carry. There are others waiting on the account of it — decisions that cannot be made until someone speaks plainly about what happened here. So I am going to speak plainly.

People have been moving through this place in all directions since it happened, and none of them know what they are walking through. I have held this long enough. It is time to put it into hands that will do something with it.
I have been the only one who saw the whole of it. That means my account is the one that will travel. I understand what I am handing you. I need you to understand it too before you take it from me.
generosity: I will tell you everything I saw — the parts that help you and the parts that do not. I have been sitting with this long enough and I would rather put it in front of you now than hold it any longer.
You have not asked me yet but I am going to tell you. There is no point waiting for the right moment when every moment it stays with only me is a moment you are working with less than you need.
Here is what happened. I will give you all of it — what I saw, when I saw it, and who else was there. You can ask me to slow down and I will slow down. But I am going to give you the full account.

wisdom: I have walked this passage more times than I can count. Before I tell you anything, tell me — what have you already seen? What you notice tells me more than your questions do.
The last group that came through here asked me where the danger was. They did not ask me what the danger wanted. I can only help the ones who ask the second question.
I know this place well enough to know that knowing is not the same as understanding. Sit with me for a moment before you move. What have your people been saying to each other since you entered?
courage: I have been to the far side of this ground twice. The second time I knew what I was walking into and I went anyway. That is why I am still here and can tell you what it holds.

Something in this place has been waiting for a long time. I felt it the first time I came. I came back to feel it again, because I needed to know whether it still had the same pull on me. It does. I am still here.

There is a stretch ahead where the ground shifts and some people stop moving. I know because I froze there myself the first time. The second time I kept walking. I will walk it with you now if you need me to.
truth: Two of the paths ahead will slow you down. One of them will stop you entirely if you are not prepared. I am not going to tell you it will probably be fine — it will not be fine unless you know what I am about to tell you.

There is a place ahead where the ground looks stable but is not. I have watched people trust it and I have watched what happens. I am telling you exactly what I saw so you do not have to find out the same way.

The passage you are planning to take is not the one you think it is. I can see by how you are standing that you have already made a decision. That decision is based on something that is not true here. Let me correct it.
humility: I know the first part of this route well. After the second ridge I am working from what others have told me, not from what I have seen myself. I will tell you clearly which is which.
There are things in this place I still do not understand, even after everything I have moved through. I can give you what I have. I would rather say where my knowledge ends than guess past it.

I have guided people through here before. Some of what I told them was right. Some of it was incomplete. I have been working out the difference ever since. I will share what I am confident in and tell you where I am less certain.
acceptance: I have brought three groups through this part of the path. Two made it through whole. One did not. I have been back since, and I am willing to go again. The path is still the path.
Some of the markers I set the last time are gone. I am not surprised. This place moves. I can work from what is still here and from what I remember. I have done it before.

I have seen what waits past the midpoint of this route. I went through it myself and some of what I was carrying did not come back with me. I am still willing to help you find the way. I know the way.
forgiveness: The last time I guided someone through here I told them the wrong thing about the crossing and they went in unprepared. I have thought about that a great deal since. I am telling you this now so you understand that I am not guessing when I speak — I have learned what I got wrong.

I made a bad call in this place once. The person I was guiding paid for it. I do not carry it the way I used to, but I have not forgotten what it cost. That is why I am careful now about what I say I know.

I was wrong about this stretch the first time I passed through it. I told the person with me that it was safer than it was. We were both lucky it turned out the way it did. I have corrected that mistake. Let me give you the version I should have given her.
compassion: Before we talk about the path, let me look at who you have brought with you. I want to know what your people have already been through — what they are carrying — before I say anything about what is ahead.

You look like you have been moving for a long time without stopping. What I have to tell you will hold for a short while. Sit. Let me see who is with you and what condition they are in before we talk about the route.

The path I know is not the same path for every group. I need to understand what your people are capable of right now, not what they were capable of when they left. What have they lost since they started moving?
empathy: The one at the back of your group — she has been keeping her distance since you arrived. I recognise that. There is a part of this passage that will ask something specific from her. I want to make sure she knows what is coming before we start.

I can see the fear in the way you are all standing. Not one person, all of you. That is something I have seen before in this place specifically. I know what caused it. I want to name it before we talk about where you need to go.

You have already lost someone, or something, before you got here. I can feel it in how quiet your group is. I am not asking you to tell me about it. I am telling you that I see it, and that the route I am about to describe will ask you to carry that weight for a while longer.
leadership: I have brought four parties through this passage. Each one was different and each one needed to hear different things. I am thinking right now about the people who will come after you — about what you will leave on this path, and what it will mean for the ones who follow.

The markers I laid down on this route are still used by people who never met me. I know that because I came back and saw them being followed. What I tell you today will outlast this conversation. I take that seriously.

I do not guide people just to get them to the other side. I guide them so they understand what they moved through well enough to guide someone else if they need to. That is the only way this knowledge survives. Let me give you enough to pass on.
generosity: I will tell you the path and I will also tell you the thing you did not know to ask about — the place halfway through where the ground looks like a dead end but is not, and where it hides the only water source for three hours in any direction.

Most people who come to me want to know the safe way through. I will give you that. I will also give you everything I know about what is on the other side, because knowing what you are walking toward changes how you walk.

Here is the route. Here is where it is harder than it looks. Here is the thing that turned back the last group that came through. And here is what I have found that they missed, which I think you are ready to use.

wisdom: I have been turning this over since before the rains came. I know what happened to me, but I do not yet know what it means — and I will not move until I do. Can you think it through with me?
There are two things people have told me about this place, and they cannot both be true. I need someone who will sit with that and not rush past it.
I came here with a question, not just a problem. I can survive the problem. What I cannot carry alone is not knowing the answer to what I am actually asking.
courage: They told me the path ahead was closed and I kept walking anyway. I am still walking. I do not need someone to tell me it will be alright — I need someone who will keep going beside me.
I have been afraid since the second day and I have not stopped. I am not asking you to make the fear go away. I am asking you not to stop when I do.
I have already crossed the part they said would break me. I am still here. But there is more ahead and I do not want to be the only one who keeps moving.
truth: People here have been kind to me, but their kindness has gaps in it — things they leave out, things they change when they think I am not listening. I need someone to tell me the real version, even if it costs me something.
I have been given three different accounts of what happened in this place. I do not know which one to carry. I would rather hear something hard and true than something soft and wrong.
I was told this passage was safe. I was told it by someone who had reasons to want me moving. What I need now is someone with no reason to soften it.
humility: I do not know how to read what is happening here. I came in with a plan and it has not held. I am telling you this before you waste time assuming I know more than I do.
There is something in this place I do not have the skill to handle, and I have known it since the first hour. I am not pretending otherwise. Tell me what you can actually do.
I have gotten myself this far, but I know where my understanding runs out. I know what is past that edge. I need someone who can go past it.
acceptance: The person I was supposed to meet here — she is not coming. That is settled in me now. Tell me what is still possible from where I am, not from where I planned to be.
I lost the route two days back. I am not looking to recover it. I am looking to find a different way forward from where I actually am standing right now.
The thing I came to protect is already gone. I know that. I am not asking you to change it. I am asking you to help me decide what I do with what is left.
forgiveness: I am here because I trusted someone I should not have. I know that now. I am not asking you to tell me it was not my fault — I know the part that was. I just need you not to keep adding to it.
I made a decision four days ago that put me on this road, and I have been carrying that decision every step. I do not need your judgment. I have enough of my own.
I chose wrong and now I am here. That is done. What I need from you is someone who will help me move from here without adding the weight of what I should have done.
compassion: There is a child at the edge of this stage who has not moved in two days. I have not been able to reach her and I cannot leave her here. My own situation can wait.
The one who brought me to this place — she is hurt. She keeps telling me she is not, but I have been watching her and I know what that kind of stillness means. Help her first.
I am not the only one who needs help here. There is a woman a half-day behind me on this path who has less than I have. I can last longer. Find her first.
empathy: You have come a long way to get here — I can see it in how you are carrying yourselves. Before I tell you what I need, are all of you still whole?
I have watched you since you came into view and I know something happened on the road before this. I am not going anywhere until you tell me what it was.
You are not moving the way people move when they are well. What did this place cost you to get here? I need to know before I ask you for anything more.
leadership: There are four others following my lead in this place and they are watching me right now to see what I do next. What I need from you has to be something I can take back and hold steady in front of them.
I have been the one holding this together for six days. The others do not know how thin that hold is. What I need from you has to work, because if I fall, they fall with me.
I cannot show uncertainty in front of the people who are depending on me here. Tell me plainly what you can do and what you cannot — I will carry the rest.
generosity: Before you ask me what I need — I know which paths ahead are still clear. I will tell you now. That knowledge is yours whether you help me or not.
I have water and I have a map of this sector. Take both. You will need them before I will. When you have heard what I need, you will understand why I can spare them.
I am going to tell you where the danger is before I say anything about myself. You should know it whether you stay or go. After that, if you can hear me out, I will tell you the rest.

wisdom: I have been sitting with this for a long time — what happened, what it means, what a fair resolution looks like. I am not here to argue. I am here because I have worked it out and I need someone to work through it with me.

Before you say anything, understand that I have already considered the other side of this claim. I know what they will say. I am asking you to tell me where my reasoning breaks, if it does — because I cannot find where it does.

I came back three times before I decided to come forward. Each time I thought of another reason why I might be wrong. I no longer believe I am wrong. But I want to hear what you see that I might have missed.
courage: They told me this place was not safe to come back to after what I said. I said it anyway. I am saying it again now. What I am owed does not become less true because claiming it is dangerous.
I have been told twice that this claim will cost me more than it is worth. I am standing here. I will keep standing here. What it costs me is not the question.
Everyone who knows what happened has gone quiet. I am not going quiet. I want what I came for, and I want to look the people in front of me in the face while I ask for it.
truth: What was said about me was not true. I need you to know that before anything else. I am not asking you to take my word over theirs — I am asking you to sit with the actual facts and tell me what they say.
Someone changed the account of what happened. It is a different story now than the one I lived through. I am not leaving until the original version is back on the table.
There are two versions of this story and only one of them is accurate. I know which one. I am here because I will not let the wrong one stand.
humility: I do not have everything here. I know that. What I have is enough to know something was taken from me, but I am asking for fairness, not a verdict. I want someone to look at it honestly.

Maybe I have some of this wrong. I am saying that plainly. I am not coming to you with certainty — I am coming to you with what I know and what I do not know, and I am asking you to help me understand what I cannot see.

I am not going to pretend I have the full picture. I have my piece of it. What I am asking for is not for you to believe me completely — it is for you to take what I have brought seriously enough to look.
acceptance: I know I am not getting back what it was before. I made my peace with that a long time ago. What I am asking for is what is still possible — not what should have been, just what can be done now.
The best of this is already gone. I am not here for the best of it. I am here for the part that is still left to settle, and I want to settle it before that is gone too.
I am not asking for more than what remains. I already know what is lost. This is about what is still standing, and I want to be heard on that before it also slips away.
forgiveness: I am not here to punish anyone. I want you to understand that first. What was done to me was real and it was wrong, and I am asking for it to be acknowledged — not avenged. Just seen.
I have decided not to carry this as a wound. But deciding that does not mean pretending it did not happen. I am here because it happened and someone needs to say so out loud.
The harm is done. I am not asking for it to be undone. I am asking for the people in front of me to look at it clearly and say: yes, that happened, that was real. That is all I need from this.
compassion: I am not only here for myself. There are others behind this claim who cannot be here — who do not have the standing to come forward or the means to press it. I am pressing it for them.

What I am asking for touches more than just my situation. There are people who have been waiting on this outcome who you will not see. I want you to keep them in your mind while you decide how to meet me.
If it were only about me, I might have let it go. It is not only about me. The people it also affects are why I kept coming back when it would have been easier to stop.
empathy: I can see you have come from somewhere difficult. I am not going to ignore that. I am still going to ask for what I came for — but I want you to know I see what you are carrying before I add to it.
You look like people who have already had to weigh too much today. I notice that. What I am bringing you is not light. I am going to ask it of you anyway, but I am asking it knowing what it costs.
I am not going to pretend I do not notice what this is for you. I do notice. And I still need this resolved — but I would rather do it in a way that does not make things worse for everyone here.
leadership: I do not speak only for myself. The people behind this claim sent me because they needed someone to stand at the front of it. I will not waste what they put in my hands by being timid about it.
There are people who depend on how this conversation ends. They are not here. I am here for them. That is the weight I am carrying and I want you to understand that before you respond.
I am representing more than my own name in this. The position I am holding is not just mine to give up or negotiate away. I need you to know what you are actually dealing with before we go further.
generosity: I have already given something toward this. I brought it in good faith before I knew how things would go. I am here now asking for what was agreed to in return. I am not asking for more than what I offered.
I came with something. I put it forward and I did not hold it back. I am standing here now because I held up my side and I need the same in return — not more, exactly what was agreed.
What I offered was real and it cost me something. I am not coming to you empty-handed and I am not coming asking for charity. I am asking for what the exchange was worth.

wisdom: I have been counting the paths in and out of this place since I arrived. There are fewer than people think, and two of them close at dusk. What have you noticed?

Something about the way this situation has been arranged does not match the story I was given before I came here. I have been sitting with that for two days. I want to know if your reading matches mine.

I do not move until I understand the ground. I have been watching this approach for long enough to see the pattern in it. You have been here a shorter time than I have. What have you seen that I might have missed?
courage: I was told this place would be abandoned by now. It is not. I have been here through three nights and I am still here. I need to know if you will hold the same ground when it asks something of you.
Most of the people who came through here turned back before they reached this point. I did not turn back. I notice you did not either. That is enough for me to want to know more about you.
I have been pushing further into this place than I was supposed to go. The reason I went further is still ahead of me. I am asking if you are the kind of people who finish what they started.
truth: I will tell you what this place actually is, not what it is being called. I have watched three groups come through here with the wrong information, and none of them fared well. What I tell you may not make this easier. But it will make it accurate.

What people have been saying about this is not what is happening here. I have been close enough to see the difference. I am not asking you to take my word for it — I am asking you to let me show you what I have seen and then tell me what you see.
I have already told two other parties the truth about what happened here. Neither of them wanted it. I will tell you anyway, and then I will leave the decision to you.
humility: I have been working this approach alone for days and I have reached the limit of what one person can know from one position. I am not asking to be in charge of this. I am asking whether what I know and what you know together gets us further than either of us separately.
I came here with a plan. The plan is incomplete — I can see that now. I know this terrain better than most, but I do not know what you know, and I have stopped pretending that is enough.

I can cover this ground on my own up to a point. I have already found that point. What I am proposing is not that you follow me — it is that we figure out together what neither of us has managed alone.
acceptance: I came here with someone who is not with me now. I have stopped looking back at where that led and started looking at what is still in front of me. I need company for what is still in front of me. I think you might be it.

My first plan for this place did not survive the first day. I am working on something different now — smaller, but real. I am looking for people who can operate in what is actually here, not what they hoped it would be.

I have already grieved what I came here for. What I am doing now is different — it is what becomes possible after you stop fighting the shape of things. I want to know if you have found that shape yet or if you are still fighting it.
forgiveness: The person who sent me here gave me the wrong information — deliberately, I think. I have decided that is not the thing I am going to carry through this place. I am carrying what I came to do instead. I want to know if you are still carrying the right things too.

Something happened here before we arrived that made this ground harder than it should be. I know who caused it and I have already decided what I am going to do with that knowledge — which is nothing, for now. I need people who can make the same decision.

I have dealt with people connected to what you are walking into, and it did not go well. I am telling you that so you know I am not coming to this clean. But I am coming to it clear, and clear is what matters here.
compassion: The one in your group who has been quiet since before you got here — I have been watching. I recognise that kind of quiet. I want to keep going, but I am also asking because I want to know if she is going to be alright.

I have been watching how you move together. There is one among you carrying more weight than the others know. I am not pointing this out to slow things down. I am pointing it out because I have been in that position and no one said anything, and it cost us.

I noticed one of yours looked back twice at the last position. Not scouting — looking back for something. I have walked with people in that state before. I want to know if she is steady enough for what is coming, because I will walk differently depending on the answer.
empathy: I know what it is to arrive somewhere and not have enough to work with. I have been in that position in places much worse than this one. I am not offering help from above you — I am offering it from beside you, because I know what you are standing in right now.

The situation you are in has a specific kind of pressure to it — I have felt that pressure before, in a different place with different stakes. I am not assuming your experience is mine. I am saying I have a shape for what you are navigating, and that shape might be useful.

I came through something like this two years ago. Not the same — nothing is the same — but close enough that I recognise the part you are at right now. I am not going to tell you it resolves. I am going to tell you I know what helps in the middle of it.
leadership: I have been managing the movement of three other people through this place for the past day and a half. I can keep doing that, but there is a gap in what I can cover and it is going to matter soon. I am looking for an anchor on the other side of it.

I have people depending on me to read this situation correctly. I have read it correctly so far. But what is coming requires more than one direction at once, and I am not willing to guess at the part I cannot see. That is why I am standing here talking to you instead of moving.

There is something I need to hold together until we get through this point, and I am holding it. I am not asking you to take it over. I am asking if you can hold something adjacent so that I do not have to split my attention at the moment when I cannot afford to.
generosity: There is a cache two hours from here that I stocked before I knew how long I was going to be in this place. I have more than I need now. I am telling you where it is regardless of what you decide about walking with me — but I wanted you to know it before we talk about anything else.

I have a route marked that avoids three of the worst approaches. I mapped it for myself and I mapped it well enough that it will work for you too. Take it. Use it. And when you have decided what you think of the person who gave it to you, come back and tell me.

I gathered information about this place over several days that most people would not share freely. I am going to share it with you now, before you have agreed to anything, because I think you need it more than I need a guarantee from you.
